summary: Checks whether a value is a number with a fractional part.
description: JavaScript has one numeric type, so `1.0` and `1` are the same value: the question answered is whether a fraction survives at runtime, not how the literal was written. The infinities have no fraction and are excluded.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is a number with a fractional part; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
isFloat(1.5); // => true
isFloat(-0.1); // => true
isFloat(42); // => false
isFloat(1.0); // => false
isFloat(Infinity); // => false
isFloat("1.5"); // => false
```
